severity_rationale: C4 Low/QA: 'State handling issues.' Operational rigidity — bootstrap-stuck-at-zero and stuck-above-sustainable states can arise, but no funds are lost or stranded (rewardBudget is preserved; conservation holds). Missing owner recovery path is a design gap, not a theft or value-leak path. Classified Low because the primary trigger is owner misconfiguration (reckless-admin-adjacent) even though the contract offers no recovery path; the user-observable harm is zero-emission phases rather than asset loss.
title: Monotonic-upward invariant combined with integer-floor candidate traps rewardRate below usable levels with no owner recovery path
description: _applyAsymmetricWindow computes candidate = rewardBudget / windowDuration with integer division, and the monotonic-upward invariant means rewardRate can only increase within a live schedule. Two related failure modes fall out of this: (1) Bootstrap-stuck-at-zero: with the default 540-day window (~46.6M seconds), any rewardBudget < windowDuration yields candidate = 0. On bootstrap (windowEnd == 0, scheduleExpired true), the reset branch sets rewardRate = 0 and windowEnd = now + windowDuration. The under-refill branch's `rewardRate > 0` guard then blocks any further adjustment, so successive small top-ups accumulate rewardBudget but never unlock emissions until a single top-up brings candidate > 0. (2) Stuck-above-sustainable: if a topUp accidentally sets rate too high and stakers drain rewardBudget before windowEnd, emissions stop but the schedule is still nominally alive. Owner cannot lower rate: topUp only raises rate (candidate <= current leaves rate unchanged), setWindowDuration is config-only (see DEDUP-001), and there is no resetRate admin path. The owner must wait for windowEnd or inject a huge new amount that hits the reset branch.
attack_path:
Bootstrap-stuck: 1) Deploy with windowDuration = 540 days. 2) Owner calls topUp(1_000_000). 3) candidate = 1_000_000 / 46_656_000 = 0; reset branch sets rewardRate = 0, windowEnd = now + 540 days. 4) Owner calls topUp(500_000). 5) candidate still 0; rewardRate is 0 so under-refill branch skipped. 6) Budget accumulates but no emissions until a single top-up crosses candidate >= 1.

Stuck-above: 1) Owner accidentally tops up with a very large amount and short windowDuration; rate is now large. 2) Stakers drain rewardBudget before windowEnd. 3) Emissions stop, rate is still nominally nonzero. 4) Owner cannot lower rate or force a reset; setWindowDuration doesn't mutate rate; only recourse is waiting or a new giant inflow that trips reset at new parameters.
impact: Operational rigidity on both ends. No direct fund loss — conservation still holds — but stakers experience zero-emission phases the owner cannot correct on-chain. Combined with pause and the dispatcher-hook flow, owner has limited tools to recover from misconfiguration.
recommendation: Three-part fix: (1) Relax the `rewardRate > 0` gate in the under-refill branch so that when rewardRate is 0 and the schedule has not expired, a non-zero inflow triggers a recomputation of candidate against the new cumulative budget. (2) Add an owner-only resetSchedule() (or an explicit flag on setWindowDuration) that allows the reset branch to fire unconditionally with sanity-checked parameters. (3) Either enforce a minimum bootstrap top-up (e.g. amount >= windowDuration) or document the edge case explicitly.

sanitization.rationale: Root cause is _applyAsymmetricWindow logic in NFTStaker.sol. Not a simple admin mistake — the contract offers no admin-mistake recovery path even if the owner acts in good faith.
